sample_notification.qualification: Fully styled and enlarged-inspected draft; not final-quality approval.

print_scale: 794-pixel maximum width per diagram, approximately A5 landscape width at 96 dpi; Desktop PNGs are content-cropped.

findings: URL permission is disconnected; native file permission is only a footer note.
The three-row arrangement does not expose all five grounded capability branches.
Workflow-to-leaf routing crosses the Prepare context and Reserve run cards.
Validate/apply-to-commit routing crosses Prepared writeback and obscures relationship ownership.
Three rows are readable but their channel boundaries are stated only in the footer.
Generic square AW icons remain placeholders rather than a finished product-specific icon inventory.
The serpentine return path is readable, but worker/AgentHost ownership needs explicit grouped boundaries.
The bridge is represented by a Pod icon although it is a logical runtime component.
Before/Now rows lack explicit enclosing worker and pod boundaries.
The command connector label consumes nearly the whole inter-card gutter.
Worker persistence crosses AgentHost, visually suggesting pod-to-database ownership.
HPA and Deployment use Pod icons; the PostgreSQL icon reads as a circle rather than a database.
Database acknowledgement crosses RecordNext and EF append.
Replica poll routes cross browser cards and share a rail, visually suggesting direct browser database access.
Person icons conflate software watchers with human actors.
The expires edge starts at A renews and ends at A stops renewing, reversing the causal order of stop then expiry.
Lease ownership and renewal are not visibly connected; Pod icons do not identify worker processes precisely.
Vault-to-CSI routing crosses authorization cards and their labels.
ServiceAccounts, CSI and workloads all use the same Pod icon despite distinct resource types.
Cross-row apply and CRDs connectors pass through preceding cards.
Namespace, storage, Service and rollout objects need correct native resource classifications rather than generic Pod icons.
API/MCP branch rails overlap the HTTPS/select route and cross Gateway/client cards.
Backend Services use Pod icons, conflating service selection with pod execution.
Observe, reject and probe connectors cross content cards instead of using phase gutters.
Approved publication combines Service/HTTPRoute creation behind a Pod icon.
Grant/reject return branches overprint the POST/request rail and cross tool/API cards.
The software start path is represented by a network-router icon without a clear component boundary.
Windows/Linux selection and unavailable branches share a rail and cross the Windows card.
This routing suggests a Windows-to-Linux chain despite the footer correctly saying they are alternatives.
Cleanup alternatives are detached from the execution flow.
Production preview lookup is an isolated card outside the retained command-path takeaway; keep that distinction inline.
The sandbox controller is not a Pod and needs an appropriate native classification.
Read-only/writable and equal/changed-tree branches are mostly disconnected.
The missing branch connectors hide the materialization-to-publication lifecycle even though card text describes it.
The progress return rail crosses dispatch and child-executor cards.
Claim binding and setup are represented as Pods rather than separate state transitions.
Launch and ready rails cross launch/configuration cards.
Configuration guards are disconnected from the route/state they constrain.
Unknown fallback routing crosses the API approval card.
Request/result arrows between the HTTP client and pod gate overlap, preventing a clean two-way trace.
The durable gate's database-style circle does not communicate a gate decision.
Flat cards do not depict two container/PID boundaries and the narrower child mount view.
A mount-view card has a spawn arrow, incorrectly turning a boundary into the spawning process.
Pod symbols are used for containers and an IPC volume; the Kata boundary is an isolated cloud card.

qualification: Actual print-scale and enlarged inspection of all 20 first-upgrade PNGs; not a correction pass or final arrow trace.
